title: Incremental validation & provenance envelope for streamed structured outputs and tool handoffs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define acceptance criteria and a rollout plan for an extensible ‘provenance envelope’ wrapping structured streaming emissions and tool-call payloads. Purpose: enable progressive (per-chunk) validation, consumer-driven schema adaptation, and reliable error reconciliation when partial objects are emitted or tool-handshakes fail.
background: Customer feedback and internal evals show two recurring problems: 1) downstream consumers crash or mis-handle partially emitted structured objects during long-running streams; 2) tool invocation semantics diverge when the model switches variants mid-stream or when networked tool endpoints return partial failures. Existing acceptance documents cover schema handshakes and idempotent tool calls, but do not prescribe provenance metadata, per-chunk validation levels, or a consumer-driven adaptation flow for compatible schema evolution.
goals: Introduce a small JSON envelope schema (provenance + schema_version + chunk_seq + validation_hint) that can be attached to each streamed chunk or tool-call payload
Specify acceptance criteria for progressive validation: consumers can choose to accept partial chunks based on validation_hint (none, soft, strong) and still reason about final object integrity
Define deterministic reconciliation rules when a later chunk modifies fields emitted earlier (last-write semantics, patch merges)
Provide operational signals (metrics and traces) for schema-mismatch events, chunk rejections, and tool-handshake fallbacks
Enable a staged rollout with a compatibility mode so older clients ignore the envelope if unrecognized
non_goals: Redesign of existing function-calling RPC layer (we only add an envelope layer on top)
Full automatic migration of arbitrary consumer JSON schemas (we support hints and adaptation paths)
Guaranteeing semantic correctness for every possible consumer implementation
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format: every streamed structured chunk and every tool-call payload MUST optionally include a top-level string field 'rwi_provenance' whose value is a base64-encoded JSON string containing: schema_id, schema_version, chunk_seq (int), chunk_finality (enum: partial|final), validation_hint (enum: none|soft|strict), origin_variant (string), and optional signature (hex). Clients MUST gracefully ignore the field if unrecognized.

Progressive validation behavior: when validation_hint=soft consumers may accept missing fields but must log a metric 'schema.partial.accept' with labels {schema_id, consumer_version}. When validation_hint=strict the server must not mark the chunk as accepted until per-chunk validation rules pass or a documented fallback is used.

Deterministic merge rules: if the same JSON path is emitted in multiple chunks, the platform must apply last-write-wins at the chunk_seq level except for arrays explicitly marked with 'merge_strategy=concat'. Merge policy MUST be documented and enforced by the streaming SDK.

Tool-call idempotency and provenance: all tool invocation payloads must include the envelope with an invocation_id (UUID) and origin_variant; if a retry occurs the invocation_id MUST remain constant to enable idempotent server-side handling. Retries must be visible in traces and telemetry.

Error reconciliation: if a downstream tool returns a transient error mid-stream, the runtime must emit an error-chunk with chunk_finality=partial and error_code mapping (transient|permanent). Acceptance requires that consumers receive a clear terminal chunk with chunk_finality=final or a documented fallback invocation within N seconds (configurable; default 5s).

Backward compatibility: older clients that do not parse 'rwi_provenance' must continue receiving raw content; acceptance requires that the runtime supports a compatibility flag 'envelope_opt_out' during rollout for 2 release cycles.

Testability: every new schema_version must include an automated compatibility test that validates at least three consumer SDK versions and two simulated network failure modes before promotion to default.

Observability: emitted metrics for schema_mismatch, chunk_rejected, tool_retry, and finality_missing; alerts configured for schema_mismatch rate >0.5% over 10m in production with customer_traffic>100 requests/min
test_cases: Streamed partial object where final chunk patches earlier fields: verify last-write semantics and that finality=final is delivered
Consumer with 'soft' validation accepts partials: verify 'schema.partial.accept' metric and that no data loss occurs after final chunk
Tool invocation with transient failure: runtime emits error-chunk, retries with same invocation_id, and consumer observes idempotent effect
Incompatible consumer (no envelope): confirm payloads are still parseable and the envelope is ignored without breaking existing behavior
Simulate network partition where final chunk is lost: validate fallback policy triggers within configured timeout and an alert is recorded
api_contract_changes: Add optional 'rwi_provenance' top-level envelope field to streaming protocol and tool-call payload schemas
Document 'validation_hint' and 'chunk_finality' semantics in public API docs and SDK typing
Expose 'envelope_opt_out' rollout flag in Console for Customer Admins to toggle compatibility mode
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-schema_id heatmap and 95th percentile chunk-latency during streaming
Alert: page if rwi_schema_mismatch_count > 0.5% over 10m for any customer with >100rps, otherwise create Sev2 incident ticket
Audit logs: record provenance envelopes for 30 days in Private deployments and 7 days in hosted by default
rollout_plan: Feature gated: default OFF for all tenants. Enable in internal staging first with simulated consumers (2 weeks).
Canary cohort: enable for 5% of production tenants with envelope_opt_out=false and monitor metrics for 7 days.
Compatibility window: after successful canary, expand to 50% and keep envelope_opt_out flag available for 2 releases. Deprecate flag after user communications and SDK upgrades.
Final enforcement: require SDK v2.1+ for strict validation modes and remove envelope_opt_out after deprecation period
dependencies: ENG-1842 (streaming-sdk): add per-chunk envelope parser and merge helpers
ENG-2267 (runtime): chunk_seq ordering guarantees and merge enforcement
PM-10823 (docs): update public API contract for provenance envelope
DES-512 (console-ux): controls for 'envelope_opt_out' toggle and rollout visualization
